I went to school for a few years, but I learned farming from my father here in Mwanza. I grow cassava on this plot because it survives when the rains are poor, and since I own the land I spread cow manure before planting — my two cows give me enough, and cassava likes it. I will not buy chemical fertilizer for cassava; that cash is for school fees, and none of my neighbors use it on tubers anyway. I use my own cuttings from last season, I do not spray anything, I have no water for irrigation, and my wife and I will do most of the work — though I will hire two young men for five days each when the roots are ready to dig.
